docs.t: Standard takeoff minimums (aircraft with 2 engines or less)?
docs.x: Standard takeoff minimums (aircraft with 2 engines or less)? 1 sm visibility, or RVR 5000 . Defined as 1 sm visibility or RVR 5000 for aircraft having 2 engines or less. Takeoff Minimums

docs.t: Published takeoff mins exceed 1 sm / RVR 5000 and no special procedure (e.g. RNP departure) is available. May you depart below the published mins?
docs.x: Published takeoff mins exceed 1 sm / RVR 5000 and no special procedure (e.g. RNP departure) is available. May you depart below the published mins? No. Takeoff in weather less than published minimums shall not be made. When published takeoff minimums are greater than 1 sm or RVR 5000, and a special procedure (e.g., RNP departure) is not available or prescribed, takeoff in weather less than published minimums shall not be made. Takeoff Minimums

docs.t: At what visibility must the Captain make the takeoff?
docs.x: At what visibility must the Captain make the takeoff? Any time visibility is less than or equal to 1/4 sm or RVR 1600 . Any time the visibility is less than or equal to 1/4 sm or 1600 RVR, the Captain will make the takeoff. Takeoff Minimums

docs.t: Controlling visibility priority order for takeoff?
docs.x: Controlling visibility priority order for takeoff? RVR > RVV > ICAO RVR > prevailing. If RVR is reported it controls for that runway; otherwise use prevailing visibility. Visibility types (5.4.1): 1. Runway Visual Range (RVR); 2. Runway Visibility Value (RVV); 3. ICAO Runway Visual Range; 4. Prevailing Visibility. If RVR is reported, it controls for the specified runway; otherwise, use prevailing visibility in the absence of RVR. Takeoff Minimums

docs.t: When is a takeoff alternate required?
docs.x: When is a takeoff alternate required? When reported departure weather is below the approach landing minimums for the runway of intended use ( excluding SA CAT I or CAT II/III ), or conditions exist that would preclude a return . MEL note: with the LLM downgraded to CAT I (MEL 05-10-01A), CAT II/III and autolands are not used, so weather below CAT I minimums then drives a takeoff alternate. A takeoff alternate is required when the reported weather at the departure airport is below the approach landing minimums for the runway of intended use, excluding any SA CAT I or CAT II/III approaches or conditions that exist that would preclude a return. Takeoff Alternate

docs.t: Maximum distance from the departure airport to a takeoff alternate (787)?
docs.x: Maximum distance from the departure airport to a takeoff alternate (787)? 393 nm. Takeoff alternates must be within the following distance: 787 - 393 nm. (FOM 5.4.2) Takeoff Alternate

docs.t: What weather must a takeoff alternate meet?
docs.x: What weather must a takeoff alternate meet? The same requirements as the Alternate for Destination weather (the derived Ops Spec C055 alternate minimums). Takeoff alternate airport weather must meet the same requirements as the Alternate for Destination Weather (see 8.2.2.1 - Destination Alternate Airport Weather Requirements). Takeoff Alternate

docs.t: As a High Minimums Captain (under 100 hr PIC in type), when is a takeoff alternate required?
docs.x: As a High Minimums Captain (under 100 hr PIC in type), when is a takeoff alternate required? If departure reported weather is below published CAT I DH +100 ft AND published CAT I visibility +1/2 sm . Under Exemption 5549 an HMC may fly CAT I to published minima (autopilot coupled to DH), and SA CAT I / SA CAT II / CAT II per FOM 3.16.2. CAT III requires 100 hr PIC in type , not reducible (FOM 3.15). Required if departure airport reported weather is below published Category I approach DH plus 100 ft and published Category I approach visibility minimums plus 1/2 sm. High Minimums Captain

docs.t: 787 takeoff below RVR 500 (150 m). What governs?
docs.x: 787 takeoff below RVR 500 (150 m). What governs? Use the Takeoff Low Visibility Card in the PRC, and the HGS/HUD Takeoff Briefing Card . New in Rev 125: this was 737-only through 124.2; the 787 is now included. MEL note: the HUD low visibility takeoff function may be deferred only when takeoff minima do not require it (MEL 31-61-14B); with it deferred, below-RVR-500 takeoffs are not available. (737/787) For takeoffs less than 500 RVR (150 m), see Takeoff Low Visibility Card in PRC. Table row: (737/787) <500 (150 m) - SEE HGS/HUD TAKEOFF BRIEFING CARD. Takeoff Minimums

docs.t: Within the contiguous 48 (or from AK / Mexico / Central America / Canada / Caribbean), when is no destination alternate required?
docs.x: Within the contiguous 48 (or from AK / Mexico / Central America / Canada / Caribbean), when is no destination alternate required? Destination weather at ETA +/- 1 hour forecast at least 2000 ft ceiling and 3 sm visibility. The 2 sm more than the lowest applicable minimums additive and the more-than-one-runway requirement apply to Alaska destinations, not the contiguous 48. Destination weather reports or forecast or any combination of them indicate at the estimated time of arrival, +/- one hour, conditions will be at least 2000 ft ceiling and 3 sm visibility. (FOM 8.2.3, Within Contiguous 48 States row. The 2 sm additive appears only in the Alaska rows.) Destination Alternate

docs.t: Flag operation (excluding A012): no-alternate ceiling and visibility requirement?
docs.x: Flag operation (excluding A012): no-alternate ceiling and visibility requirement? Ceiling: straight-in available, at least 1500 ft above the lowest published IAP min or 2000 ft above field elev , whichever is higher; if circling required, 1500 ft above the lowest circling MDA . Vis: 3 sm or 2 sm more than the applicable min, whichever greater, ETA +/- 1 hr. Ceiling at or above either of the following: If a circling approach is required, 1500 ft above the lowest circling MDA. If a straight-in approach is available, at least 1500 ft above the lowest published instrument approach minimum or 2000 ft above airport elevation, whichever is higher. Three miles visibility or two miles more than the applicable visibility minimum, whichever is greater, for the instrument approach procedure to be used. Destination Alternate

docs.t: When is a destination alternate ALWAYS required, regardless of forecast?
docs.x: When is a destination alternate ALWAYS required, regardless of forecast? Any Flag flight planned over 6 hours flight time; and When thunderstorms or volcanic ash are forecast in the TAF at the ETA. An alternate airport must be listed on the release prior to dispatch when thunderstorms or volcanic ash are forecast in the TAF at the ETA. / Per 14 CFR 121.621, an alternate is required for any Flag flight more than six hours flight time as planned on the Flight Plan. Destination Alternate

docs.t: Derived alternate minimums, ONE nav facility (straight-in non-precision, CAT I, or circling). Additives?
docs.x: Derived alternate minimums, ONE nav facility (straight-in non-precision, CAT I, or circling). Additives? Add 400 ft to MDA(H)/DA(H), and add 1 sm (1600 m) to the landing minimum. MEL note: with an expired nav database (MEL 05-34-01), RNP and RNAV procedures are not permitted, so plan approaches on ground-based NAVAIDs. At least one operational navigational facility providing a straight-in non-precision approach, a CAT I precision approach, or a circling maneuver: Add 400 ft to MDA(H) or DA(H), as applicable. Add 1 sm or 1600 m to landing minimum. Alternate Minimums

docs.t: Derived alternate minimums, TWO facilities to different suitable runways (two approach ends). Additives?
docs.x: Derived alternate minimums, TWO facilities to different suitable runways (two approach ends). Additives? Add 200 ft to the higher DA(H)/MDA(H) of the two, and add 1/2 sm (800 m) to the higher authorized landing minimum of the two. At least two operational navigational facilities, each providing a straight-in non-precision or precision approach to different, suitable runways (two approach ends): Add 200 ft to higher DA(H) or MDA(H). Add 1/2 sm or 800 m to higher authorized landing minimum of two approaches used. Alternate Minimums

docs.t: Do the Jeppesen 'For Filing As Alternate' minimums apply to our operations? How are additives rounded?
docs.x: Do the Jeppesen 'For Filing As Alternate' minimums apply to our operations? How are additives rounded? No , they do not apply. Use the derived table. Additives apply only to the height (H) value, rounded up to the next 100 ft . Wind including gust must be forecast within limits. The minimums depicted in 'For Filing As Alternate' listed on the Jeppesen 10-9/10-9A pages do not apply to our operations. Additives are applied only to the height value (H) rounded up to the next 100-ft value (if not a multiple of 100) to determine the required ceiling. Wind including gust must be forecast to be within operating limits. Alternate Minimums

docs.t: When is a second (marginal) alternate required?
docs.x: When is a second (marginal) alternate required? Destination ceiling (if required) and/or visibility is at or below CAT I minimums for the intended runway/approach, AND the first alternate is at alternate minimums (ceiling OR visibility). Also for a flag/supplemental flight to an international airport missing METAR info (both alternates need a complete METAR and TAF). Marginal: Destination airport weather has a ceiling (if required) AND/OR the visibility is at or below CAT I minimums for the intended runway and approach to be used. Alternate airport weather is marginal when either the ceiling OR visibility is at alternate minimums. A second alternate is required for a flag or supplemental flight if dispatching to an international airport that is missing information in the METAR per Ops Spec A010(e). Both destination alternates must have a complete METAR and TAF. Second Alternate

docs.t: When may you begin the final approach segment? What if a below-min report arrives after?
docs.x: When may you begin the final approach segment? What if a below-min report arrives after? Reported weather must be at or above the approach visibility mins. Do not begin the final approach segment unless the latest RVR, visibility, or ceiling (if required) is at or above authorized mins. If a below-min report arrives after the final segment has begun, you may continue to DA/DH or MDA . The reported weather at the destination must be at or above the visibility minimums prescribed for the approach. Do not begin the final approach segment of an instrument approach procedure unless the latest reported RVR, visibility, or ceiling (if required) is at or above the authorized minimums. If a weather report is obtained after the final approach segment of an instrument approach has been initiated, and it indicates below minimum conditions, the pilot may continue the approach to DA/DH or MDA. Approach

docs.t: Which RVR is controlling, and what is the approach visibility floor?
docs.x: Which RVR is controlling, and what is the approach visibility floor? Non-Precision and CAT I: TDZ RVR controls (Mid and Rollout are advisory; Mid may substitute if TDZ unavailable). CAT II/III: all required RVR values on the approach briefing card apply. RVR greater than 6000 is advisory only. Visibility values below 1/2 sm are not authorized for approach minimums (RVR-based CAT II/III minima below that equivalent remain authorized). TDZ RVR reports are controlling. Mid RVR and Rollout RVR reports (if available) are advisory. Mid RVR report may be substituted for the TDZ RVR if the TDZ RVR report is not available. RVR values greater than 6000 are advisory only. Visibility values below 1/2 sm are not authorized and shall not be used for approach minimums. Approach

docs.t: Takeoff/landing prohibited: wind, crosswind, braking action?
docs.x: Takeoff/landing prohibited: wind, crosswind, braking action? Steady-state wind greater than 50 kt . Crosswind exceeds fleet-specific manual limits (787 per FCOM/AOM - not on this sheet). Braking action NIL or RWYCC 0 on any portion of the runway. Takeoffs and landings are prohibited when: Steady-state wind velocity is greater than 50 kts. Crosswinds exceed limits in fleet-specific manuals. Braking action is NIL or the RWYCC is 0 on any portion of the runway. Prohibited

docs.t: Takeoff/landing prohibited: 787 contaminated surface width, thunderstorms, freezing rain, icing?
docs.x: Takeoff/landing prohibited: 787 contaminated surface width, thunderstorms, freezing rain, icing? 787 contaminated prepared surface width less than 45 m (148 ft) . TS at or near the airport unless runway and flight path (incl missed approach) are clear of storms. Moderate or greater freezing rain (takeoff still allowed if an LWE-derived HOT is available, absent another prohibitor). Severe icing reported by a similar type or larger aircraft. Contaminated runway preparation results in an available prepared surface width of less than 45 m / 148 ft (787). Takeoffs, approaches, and landings should not be attempted when TS are reported at or near the airport unless runway of intended operation and the flight path, including missed approach, are clear of the storms. There is moderate or greater freezing rain (takeoff still allowed if an LWE-derived HOT is available, unless another prohibiting factor exists). Severe icing is reported by a similar type or larger aircraft. Prohibited

docs.t: Takeoff prohibited: contaminant depth limits?
docs.x: Takeoff prohibited: contaminant depth limits? Contaminant depth greater than 1/2 inch for wet snow, slush, or water, or greater than 4 inches for dry snow. Also: steady-state tailwind over 10 kt on a contaminated runway. Takeoffs are prohibited when: Contaminant depth is greater than 1/2 inch for wet snow, slush, or water or greater than 4 inches for dry snow. Steady-state tailwind component exceeds 10 kts on a contaminated runway. Prohibited

docs.t: Which weather report is controlling?
docs.x: Which weather report is controlling? The most recent report , including Remarks or conditional language. A verbal tower report of visibility / RVV / RVR takes precedence over METAR or ATIS. The controlling visibility for an airport, or if a particular runway is identified, is the most recent report, including Remarks or conditional language. A verbal report from a control tower that includes a visibility value, Runway Visibility (RVV) or Runway Visual Range (RVR), is controlling and will take precedence over a METAR or ATIS. Controlling Report
